report.summary: At t = 2.12 s car-1 starts braking, 2.08 s before impact, with peak deceleration 5.09 m/s^2, and impact between car-0 and car-1 is at t = 4.2 s. From t = 3.0 to 4.0 s car-0 is at 54.3 km/h (90% interval 49.9 to 60.1) and car-1 is at 31.8 km/h (90% interval 29.3 to 35.4). The s1 speed claim for the white car is not consistent with the footage, as the measured speed is 54.3 km/h (90% interval 49.9 to 60.1). The s1 claim that the light was green cannot be checked from the footage. The s2 speed claim for the blue car is consistent with the footage, and the s2 claim that the white car did not brake is consistent with the footage, with no sustained braking detected before impact.
limitations: No burned-in clock and evenly spaced file timestamps: frames the recorder dropped cannot be seen, so the speed intervals allow speeds up to about 20% higher than the file suggests.
Road calibration error: 0.499 m (how well the clicked road points fit a flat road); positions assume a flat road.

The momentum check after the impact did not balance (inconsistent): after contact the vehicles overlap in the image, so post-impact motion is not reliable. Speeds before the impact are measured separately and are not affected.

Traffic-light claims cannot be checked: 8 traffic lights in view (traffic_light-0, traffic_light-1, traffic_light-2, traffic_light-3, traffic_light-4, traffic_light-5, traffic_light-6, traffic_light-7); choose which one governs the stop line.
Measurements come from one camera; they support expert review and do not determine fault.
